video_title: Quentin Richardson reacts to OKC-Spurs Game 6 and Mitchell Robinson's injury | The Pat McAfee Show

quotes.speaker: Quentin Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs dominate Thunder in Game 6 to force Game 7
quotes.excerpt: The Spurs are what I expected them to be. They forced it to Game 7.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: The reason why today is a little bit different than some of these days coming off of an NBA playoff game, it was just an ass-beating last night. It wasn't a lot of glitz, glamour of a Game 6 forcing Game 7. It was more so just San Antonio Spurs just dominating Oklahoma City. Even doing a body check to SGA in that game as if they were sending a tone for future Game 7 as well. What are your thoughts on last night? How should we be judging this Oklahoma City team that just got smacked in Game 6 as we look ahead to Game 7 and where do you kind of sit with this Spurs team as a whole?

text_blocks.speaker: Quentin Richardson
text_blocks.text: The Spurs are what I expected them to be. They forced it to Game 7. This is what I thought this series would be, a six or seven-game series. So, we as fans get to enjoy a Game 7. The tone of this series, the way it's gone, it feels like to me it started with the first four games. Then it was home, away, home, away, home, away just winning. Right now, I feel like that's kind of where it's at. Oklahoma City kind of tuned them up the last game at home, then the Spurs come back and do the same thing. They did that the last game at home. So for me, I feel like this Game 7, everything kind of goes out the window.

quotes.speaker: Quentin Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' offensive shift to Karl-Anthony Towns as facilitator
quotes.excerpt: When they switched and started playing through Karl-Anthony Towns up top and letting him be more of a facilitator.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: Does the Knicks team, just because of how hot they've been, have a chance to win, or is there a matchup that really tells the story of, yeah, the Knicks can certainly beat either of the Western Conference teams?

text_blocks.speaker: Quentin Richardson
text_blocks.text: The key thing that happened for the Knicks is when they switched and started playing through Karl-Anthony Towns up top and letting him be more of a facilitator. I think that's opened up things for Jalen Brunson because obviously he still can get the ball and do his thing whenever, but him coming off the ball is tougher for opponents than loading up and guarding against him being iso ball. I think that's opened him up. Obviously Mikal Bridges has played a lot better. Hart is the heart of the team, and I feel like the big guys have played great for him. All things they clicked well, they clicked at the right time.

quotes.speaker: Quentin Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's dominance and officiating in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Everybody tries to do it. The only difference is some are better than others. And I guess if we want to say that, that means SGA is the best at it.
quotes.quote: It is still not new to me. Me as a fan, I watch most games in the league. I watch games every night. You can look through the game, everybody tries to do it. Everybody. You can go on YouTube now, you can make a highlight clip of any player who plays significant minutes trying to sell a call or trying to sell a foul. You can do it. I don't care who they are. Any player, they will be caught if you do it. Everybody has tried to do it. The only difference is some are better than others. And I guess if we want to say that, that means SGA is the best at it. Not only is he the best at that, he's been the best at scoring. He's been the best guy at offense, period, the last two years. He's been the most valuable player two years running.
